## vLLM Ascend v0.18.0 Release Feedback

We have released **vLLM Ascend v0.18.0**. This issue is for collecting post-release feedback from the community.

### What's New

- C8 (INT8 KV cache) is now supported for GQA attention models.
- Qwen3-VL gains stronger operator support with Flash Comm V1 and `qkv_rmsnorm_mrope`.
- Stability has been improved compared with `v0.18.0rc1`, especially for PD serving, KV Pool, Qwen3.5 on A2, and 310P graph mode.
- Ascend950 compatibility is improved for updated `npu-smi info` behavior and `SOC_VERSION` detection.

### How to Test

You can validate the final release with one of the following methods:

1. **Using Docker**
   ```bash
   docker pull quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.18.0
   ```

2. **Using pip**
   ```bash
   pip install vllm-ascend==0.18.0
   ```

3. **Building from source**
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend.git
   cd vllm-ascend
   git checkout v0.18.0
   pip install -e .
   ```

### Feedback Guidelines

Please share the following in comments if you hit issues:

- Bug reports with reproduction steps and logs
- Performance regressions compared with `v0.18.0rc1` or earlier releases
- Model-specific compatibility problems
- Documentation gaps or unclear upgrade guidance

### Environment Information

When reporting problems, please include:

```text
- vLLM Ascend version:
- vLLM version:
- CANN version:
- torch_npu version:
- Hardware (910B/910C/310P/A2/A3/950):
- OS:
- Launch command or deployment mode:
```

### Timeline

- **Final Release Date**: 2026.04.14
- **Feedback Window**: 1-2 weeks after release
- **Follow-up Fixes**: Regressions found here should be tracked for the next patch or RC

### Related Links

- [Release Checklist](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/8198)
- [Release Notes](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/user_guide/release_notes.html)
- [Documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest)
- [Releases](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/releases)

Thank you for helping improve vLLM Ascend.

issues.title: [Performance] Cache loaded Gemma RMSNorm unit-offset weights
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Gemma RMSNorm residual paths, the A5 RMSNorm adaptor, and fused Q/K normalization currently recompute `1 + weight` on each invocation. Cache the effective weight when the Norm's checkpoint loader runs and reuse it in these consumers, including Qwen3.5 and MiniMax M3 fused Q/K normalization.

The cache preserves the original parameter-dtype rounding and leaves checkpoint parameters unchanged. It is a nonpersistent buffer, refreshed in place on weight reload so captured graphs keep its storage. PyTorch state-dict loads (including `assign=True`) refresh it, and dtype/device conversion recomputes it in the destination dtype. Grad-enabled execution retains the original differentiable addition. Unprepared receivers/loaders retain runtime computation. Native Gemma kernels continue to receive raw weights.

There is no batch-size, token-count, or output-history-length threshold. Each Norm allocates one additional weight-sized buffer (4 KiB for 2048 BF16 elements). No model-runner behavior or environment variable is added. The existing Qwen3.5 patch only changes the effective-weight accessor; its lifecycle/removal rationale is recorded in the patch inventory.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Removes repeated unit-offset additions in supported inference paths. No checkpoint format or configuration change. A5 local-call measurements and exact-output checks are recorded below; model-level latency remains unmeasured.

Includes the performance release-note fragment `release_notes/fragments/21449.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Review preparation — 2026-11-12

Added an explicit `_effective_weight: torch.Tensor` declaration to resolve the CI mypy `has-type` error for the dynamically registered buffer. The error was reproduced locally before the declaration; focused mypy checks of `vllm_ascend/ops/layernorm.py` now pass for Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12 with mypy 1.11.1. Full `bash format.sh ci` and the isolated cache-lifecycle checks (13 passed, 9 subtests) were rerun successfully. This is a type-only change; the full CI matrix must rerun for the amended commit.

Rebased onto upstream `3f1de8b04de8feab92587439b24e2cbf67133720` and squashed to one signed-off commit, `a5066f13b2efc406c3c7c2c34a34806db459b8a3`. Resolved the Qwen3.5 import conflict by retaining both upstream checkpoint initialization and the cached Norm-weight accessor. `bash format.sh ci` passed all hooks; `git diff --check` and parsing of changed Python files passed.

Focused local CPU checks: **13 passed, 9 subtests passed (cache lifecycle, precision conversion, reload and compiled-consumer checks)**. These checks use real CPU PyTorch with unavailable runtime dependencies isolated or mocked; they are not the full standard test suite or NPU validation.

The A5 measurements below retain their original tested revisions and environment. No new NPU run was performed after this rebase; they must not be read as fresh full-stack measurements of this commit.

#### A5 validation supplied on 2026-11-11

Hardware-tested head (before this rebase): `466224ab39266d8b464bd783ddbfcd65bb797e48`. Baseline: `1e2557aebd28f8959a0a8895713650d60e28be6b`. These SHAs were rechecked against GitHub on 2026-11-12. Results below are from the supplied hardware run/logs, not a new NPU run during this description update.

- Ascend950PR_957b (A5); timing on idle physical NPU 1, exposed as process `npu:0`.
- CANN 9.2.0, OPP timestamp 20260928_152710304; Python 3.11.10; torch 2.10.0+cpu with torch_npu 2.10.0.post7; triton-ascend 3.6.0+dev20260923230212.
- Installed vLLM **0.30.0+empty**; container Ascend wheel 0.30.0rc2.dev227+gde8ad7b00.d20261029. Each PR's Python source was selected with an isolated worktree/PYTHONPATH, using the installed device libraries. **This is not the pinned vLLM full-stack environment shown in the bot footer.**
- Focused tests pre-imported production op registration and bypassed incompatible global conftests (`modelscope` missing for E2E; `vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_planning` missing for UT). These results do not mean the complete standard suite passed. Existing UT mocks are distinguished from real numerical kernels below.
- Synthetic inputs use shapes from a Qwen3.5-35B-A3B MXFP8 EP=1 deployment. No serving-engine/model evaluation, task accuracy, TTFT, TPOT or throughput A/B was run.

#### Correctness coverage

- **43 focused NPU tests passed**: FP16/BF16, widths 256/2048, M=1/4/16/128/1024, plain/residual output with zero tolerance, reload after graph capture, and a profiler check for removal of `aten::add`.
- **68 focused unit/adaptor tests passed**, covering supported loaders, cache lifetime and device-adaptor contracts. These bypassed incompatible global conftests.
- **16 additional real fused Q/K kernel cases**: FP16/BF16 × M=1/7/128/1024 × Qwen M-RoPE/A5 QKV RoPE SIMT. Two weight reloads per case preserved cache addresses and byte-identical graph outputs. This is kernel-contract coverage, not a complete MiniMax M3 run.
- The **40 BF16 batch/branch entries** below passed eager and graph bytewise comparisons; all seven measured rounds improved for each entry.

One plain or residual Gemma RMSNorm call, BF16 x[M,2048] and weight[2048]; not the whole layer or fused Q/K timing.

Same device/inputs and warm-up; NPU Events around warmed graph replay, excluding JIT/initial graph construction and Python single-op submission gaps. Seven alternating ABA/BAB rounds. Base/candidate latency columns are medians; reduction is the **median of paired round reductions**, so it need not equal the ratio of the two displayed medians. Positive rounds count reductions greater than zero. Negative reductions mean regression.

Decode B=1/2/4/8/16/32/64/128, L=1; prefill L=128/512/2048 at B=1/4/16, plus L=512 at B=2/8/32. M=B×L is the number of rows handled by this call, not generated output length. A whole prompt enters one local call; this does **not** test serving with chunked prefill disabled. Norm/routing/gating see flattened rows, whereas GDN/FIA receive sequence boundaries. Four independent inputs are used for stateless/FIA cases; GDN uses fixed buffers with state restored before each sampling segment. Internal FLA algorithm blocks are retained.

The original parameter cannot be freed because checkpoint/state-dict handling, cache refresh after dtype/device changes, native Gemma RMSNorm and runtime fallbacks still need it. It preserves parameter-dtype rounding and the original checkpoint parameter. Supported loader/state-dict/dtype-device transitions refresh it; direct parameter mutation after preparation does not automatically invalidate it. Parameter-only transfer/RL hot-update bypasses remain unvalidated.

A2/A3 native plain Gemma Norm still receives raw weights and is not claimed to gain from this cache. issues.body:
> Port of #19001 (`releases/v0.30.0`) to main. Same content.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Upstream vLLM gates sequence parallelism on `use_sequence_parallel_moe`, which requires an MoE checkpoint with expert parallelism. As a result, dense Qwen3.5-family checkpoints (Qwen3.5-27B / Qwen3.6-27B / **Qwen3.8-27B**, model_type `qwen3_5_text`, `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` architecture) could not run sequence parallelism on Ascend at all.

This PR extends the existing Ascend FlashComm SP switch to cover the dense Qwen3.5 family, enabled with `tensor_parallel_size > 1`, `pipeline_parallel_size == 1` and:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --additional-config '{"enable_flashcomm1": true}'
```

What changed:

- `vllm_ascend/utils.py`: new `enable_dense_sp()` predicate (TP > 1, PP == 1, `qwen3_5_text`, FlashComm switch); `enable_sp()` now covers dense models, activating the existing V1 SP infrastructure.
- `vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py`: resolves and logs the dense-SP state during config validation (the predicate lives in `vllm_ascend.utils`; not an AscendConfig field).
- `vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_qwen3_5.py`: installs a sequence-parallel `Qwen3_5DecoderLayer`:
  - hidden states / residual stay sequence-sharded; RMSNorms run on the rank-local shard;
  - attention (full attention and GDN) all-gathers before, reduce-scatters after (`o_proj` / `out_proj` flip to `reduce_results=False`);
  - dense MLP gathers around its TP-sharded weights (no replication);
  - MoE blocks keep the upstream `already_sequence_parallel=True` contract; MTP and model-level entry/exit reuse upstream wiring.
- `docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/sequence_parallelism.md`: documents the dense path.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. For dense Qwen3.5-family models with TP > 1, `enable_flashcomm1` now enables dense sequence parallelism (previously a no-op). Numerics are equivalent to the all-reduce layout. Dense SP requires `pipeline_parallel_size == 1`.

**Performance expectations:** communication volume is unchanged; gains come from elementwise work and between-layer activations shrinking to the rank-local shard. Magnitude is hardware-dependent (measurable on high-HCCS-bandwidth hardware such as 950PR/A5; may be negligible on 800I A3). Decode-heavy workloads will regress — the switch is opt-in per deployment.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests: `tests/ut/patch/worker/test_patch_qwen3_5_sp.py`.
- CPU simulation matches the all-reduce reference to fp32 rounding (rel err ~1e-7), including `T % tp != 0` padding, for TP in {2, 4}.
- E2E (CI, 2 cards): `tests/e2e/pull_request/two_card/test_qwen3_8_27b_dense_sp.py` validates eager and FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph modes via logprob consistency.
- Interfaces verified against vLLM main (24420b7a).

### Port-specific adjustments

- `enable_dsa_cp` / `flashcomm_explicitly_enabled` no longer exist on main; the dense-SP gate in `AscendConfig.derive_and_validate` reads main's `effective_flashcomm` directly.
- The `fuse_gemm_comms` graph-level MatmulReduceScatterFusionPass already exists on main, so the dense-SP docs keep referencing it (the release branch had to omit it).
- The release-branch-only `VLLM_ASCEND_ROPE_UB_SIZE_KB` env entry does not exist on main.

- [x] **Performance impact**: prefill gains are hardware-dependent (A5 measurable, A3 may be negligible). Decode will regress — opt-in per deployment.

issues.title: [RFC]: Track vLLM speculative decoding issues and fixes
issues.body:
### Motivation.

Track vLLM speculative-decoding issues, fixes and feature alignment, using upstream Issues as the primary tracking entries where available. Track Ascend workaround PRs (including later adjustments) separately from PRs that remove those workarounds.

### Proposed Change.

**1. Preserve logical dummy tokens under PIECEWISE padding**

Keep logical query counts separate from graph-padded inputs to avoid dummy-run batch mismatches and draft profiling failures.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  Issue: None.

  - [ ] Preserve dummy tokens across PIECEWISE padding: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60049

- **vLLM Ascend workarounds**

  - [x] Pre-merge workaround: preserve dummy query widths for PIECEWISE DP/MTP (narrower coverage): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18038
  - [x] v0.30.0 backport: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18108

- **vLLM Ascend workaround cleanup**

  PR: not yet linked.

**2. Avoid excessive DP draft-batch padding**

Use real request counts instead of target graph capacity when sizing adaptive DSpark draft batches.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  - [ ] Issue: DSpark draft-token inflation with DP and adaptive verification. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61806
  - [ ] Avoid target request padding in the DP drafter: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58984
  - [ ] Related fix, picked into vllm-project/vllm#58984: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61807

- **vLLM Ascend workarounds**

  - [x] Pre-merge workaround: resynchronize draft DP counts during adaptive verification: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18249
  - [x] v0.30.0 backport: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/18250

- **vLLM Ascend workaround cleanup**

  PR: not yet linked.

**3. Correct DFlash/DSpark scheduling-budget accounting**

Avoid charging the separate draft pass against the target token budget while keeping draft inputs within buffer capacity.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  - [x] Issue: overly conservative DSpark scheduling budget. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52922
  - [x] Merged: remove DFlash/DSpark draft-slot charges and cap active requests. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59468
  - [ ] Alternative: separate target and draft budgets (closed without merge). https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53080

- **vLLM Ascend workarounds**

  Local PR: not identified.

- **vLLM Ascend workaround cleanup**

  PR: not yet linked.

**4. DFlash/DSpark graph preparation and context-KV precompute**

Confirm context-KV precompute graph coverage on Ascend. Upstream already captured precompute before this PR; the new change adds conditional in-graph metadata updates and skips eager metadata rebuilds.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  Issue: None linked by the PR.

  - [x] Skip DFlash/DSpark metadata rebuilds when all draft backends support in-place updates: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60692

- **vLLM Ascend workarounds**

  To confirm: whether context-KV precompute (_precompute_context_kv) runs inside Ascend graph capture/replay, and whether the metadata-update eligibility and fallback are correctly adapted. Local PR: not yet linked.

- **vLLM Ascend workaround cleanup**

  PR: not yet linked.

**5. Skip drafting when no request can use the drafts**

Use K=0 for steps whose drafts cannot be used, including non-final prefill chunks and requests reaching max_tokens. Retain required draft KV/context updates and DP coordination.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  Issue: None.

  - [x] Merged: skip unused drafting on MRV2. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62784

- **vLLM Ascend workarounds**

  - [ ] Adapt AR prefill to forward skip_sample while preserving draft KV updates and older-baseline compatibility: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19538

  Pending NPU validation: skip_drafts/K=0 propagation, draft KV synchronization, and DP behavior. Standalone draft_model and multi-module MTP are not covered upstream.

- **vLLM Ascend workaround cleanup**

  PR: not yet linked.

**6. Batch-sharded draft logits**

Keep draft logits only on each request's verification owner rank, reducing the cache to ceil(max_num_seqs / TP) rows per rank. Draft generation remains replicated.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  Issue: None linked by the PR.

  - [x] Merged: shard draft logits cache allocation, writes and rejection-sampling reads by request owner. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63554

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  To confirm: NPU cache writers and rejection readers use the same owner/row mapping and load-time allocation. Retain the replicated fallback for sampling overrides that do not support the sharding contract. Local PR: not yet linked.

**7. PCP with DSpark for DeepSeek-V4.1**

Support fixed-length DSpark with PCP by retaining compressor rollback tails and synchronizing draft tokens/logits across PCP ranks. Adaptive verification remains unsupported in the upstream V4.1 PCP path.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  Issue: None linked by the PR.

  - [x] Merged: preserve compressor rollback state and consistent PCP draft proposals for DeepSeek-V4.1. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61994

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  To confirm: compressor ring-tail retention/publication and draft-token/logit synchronization, including partial rejection, empty ranks and decode-owner changes. Local PR: not yet linked.

**8. Include speculative drafting in bench forward**

Time target forward plus configured draft generation, including draft sampling, by default; --exclude-drafter retains target-only timing. Drafts are assumed fully accepted; target sampling, rejection sampling and CPU overhead are excluded.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  Issue: None linked by the PR.

  - [x] Merged: include MTP/EAGLE/DSpark/DFlash drafting in bench forward timing. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63622

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  To confirm: NPU graph timing covers target and drafter, with KV lookahead/state restoration and accurate timing-scope reporting. Validate included/excluded-drafter results separately from serving latency. Local PR: not yet linked.

**9. Preserve grammar-invalid drafts for rejection sampling**

Keep the first grammar-invalid draft for rejection sampling so replacement tokens use the residual distribution instead of resampling directly from the target. Failed grammar acceptance must leave matcher state unchanged.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  - [x] Issue: structured-output speculative decoding biases the sampling distribution. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60451
  - [x] Design RFC (closed): preserve the output distribution with structured outputs and speculative decoding. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62818
  - [x] Merged: preserve grammar-invalid drafts and make grammar acceptance atomic on failure. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61557
  - [ ] Alternative fix (closed without merge). https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60690

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  To confirm: trim_spec_tokens compatibility, grammar-mask generation and NPU rejection-sampler residual sampling under synchronous/asynchronous structured-output decoding. Local PR: not yet linked.

**10. MRV2 DBO with speculative decoding and DCP**

Enable DBO with speculative decoding or DCP in MRV2; PCP remains gated. Rebuild full-batch attention metadata for drafting after the microbatched target forward, and split multi-token verification batches on request boundaries using DP-agreed token counts.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  Issue: None linked by the PR.

  - [x] Merged: support MRV2 DBO with speculative decoding and DCP. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61464

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  To confirm: full-batch draft metadata/slot mappings, request-aligned verification splits and DBO thresholds for small/idle batches. Preserve per-microbatch DCP lengths and communication buffers, and validate ACL graph capture/replay consistency. Local PR: not yet linked.

**11. MTP drafts in the Transformers modeling backend**

Serve MTP drafts for Transformers-backend targets that follow the num_mtp_layers standard, using TransformersForMTP / TransformersMoEForMTP. Reuse MtpModel weight conversion and per-layer execution, selecting draft layers through spec_step_idx.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  Issue: None linked by the PR.

  - [x] Merged: support MTP drafts in the Transformers modeling backend. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61270

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  To confirm: Transformers MtpModel helper/version requirements, draft architecture routing and NPU attention/operator compatibility. Validate checkpoint loading, target embedding/LM-head sharing and multi-layer MTP selection, including last-stage draft placement with PP. Local PR: not yet linked.

**12. Per-layer fused shared expert selection**

Track layer-scoped fusion policy and checkpoint remapping in model/MTP loaders, retaining higher-precision shared experts where fusion is incompatible. Upstream fused execution uses ROCm/AITER; Ascend backend support requires separate qualification.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  Issue: None linked by the PR.

  - [x] Merged: select fused shared experts per layer and migrate model/MTP loading to the layer-set policy. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61457

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  To confirm: compatibility with fused_shared_expert_layers and the updated maybe_fuse_shared_experts API, including MTP weight/scale remapping and expert counts. Preserve Ascend-specific fusion capability checks and validate mixed-policy EP/EPLB restrictions. Local PR: not yet linked.

**13. Fuse DFlash2 candidate edge scoring**

Fuse candidate gathers, edge dot products and unary-score addition into one Triton kernel shared by Qwen DFlash2 and Beam. Scores now remain FP32.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  Issue: None linked by the PR.

  - [x] Merged: fuse DFlash2 candidate edge scoring. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64916

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  To confirm: NPU adaptation of dflash2_score_edges and the shared _score_edges interface, preserving reference casts/rounding and FP32 output. Check candidate-selection parity and ACL graph replay, and measure edge-scoring and end-to-end effects separately. Local PR: not yet linked.

**14. Fuse DeepSeek-V4.1 DSpark Markov sampling by inverse CDF**

Use the sample_sequential hook to run each draft step as the bias GEMM plus two fused kernels, sampling by inverse CDF from cached draft logits. Upstream is opt-in through dspark_fused_markov; adaptive verification, batch-sharded sampling, FP64 Gumbel and watermarking retain the default loop.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  Issue: None linked by the PR.

  - [x] Merged: fuse the NVIDIA DSpark Markov sampling loop for DeepSeek-V4.1. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64442

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  To confirm: NPU kernels and sample_sequential integration, cached-logit rounding, temperature-zero argmax and seed/position/step indexing. Validate stochastic sampling against the cached-logit distribution and preserve eligibility/fallback behavior, including the sharded-cache contract tracked in item 6. Local PR: not yet linked.

**15. XPress with Acceptance Estimator**

Feed final Jacobi-refined logits to the estimator so adaptive verification reads initialized confidence instead of collapsing to one verified token. Cover full-vocabulary and top-C paths while preserving AV-off drafting.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  Issue: None linked by the PR.

  - [x] Merged: support XPress with Acceptance Estimator. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65175

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  Track in the XPress RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/19641

  To confirm: Jacobi return-value compatibility, refined-logit request/slot mapping and confidence updates, including AV on/off correctness and NPU graph replay.

**16. Skip fully masked vocab blocks during resampling**

In MRV2 rejection sampling, skip draft-logit loads and Gumbel generation for vocab blocks whose target logits are all -inf. Enable the check only for chunks that may contain masked logits; upstream verifies bitwise-identical sampled tokens.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  No dedicated issue linked by the PR; related roadmap:
  - [ ] Q4 speculative-decoding / rejection-sampling optimization. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61024
  - [x] Merged: skip fully masked vocab blocks in the resample kernel. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65100

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  To confirm: may_mask_logits propagation and NPU resample-kernel compatibility, preserving RNG/output parity and the unmasked fallback. Measure masked and unmasked workloads separately. Local PR: not yet linked.

**17. Restore DFlash acceptance under FULL graphs**

Refresh persistent kernel block tables before FULL draft replay when eager metadata rebuilding is skipped (item 4). Split KV/kernel block sizes otherwise leave stale mappings and collapse draft acceptance; the shared DFlash-family path is affected.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  - [x] Issue: DFlash acceptance drops to near zero with FULL graphs. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63587
  - [x] Merged: map draft kernel block tables before FULL replay. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64059

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  To confirm: equivalent block-table refresh in the NPU FULL replay path, especially with split block sizes and skipped metadata builds. Compare acceptance against eager/PIECEWISE execution. Local PR: not yet linked.

**18. Separate prefill-token and decode-request graph capture sizes**

Configure prefill/mixed graphs in tokens and uniform decode graphs in requests, with a decode-token budget. Align target verification, draft graph shapes and adaptive verification with the new capture/dispatch APIs.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  No dedicated issue linked by the PR; related roadmap:

  - [ ] Q4 prefill/decode graph-size separation. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61024
  - [x] Merged: separate prefill-token and decode-request capture sizes. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63406

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  To confirm: Ascend configuration/defaults, legacy-field compatibility and ACL graph manager API alignment (decode_query_lens), including dynamic speculative decoding and adaptive verification. Size persistent outputs for the widest captured graph and retain correct padding/fallback behavior. Local PR: not yet linked.

**19. Muse Spark specialized decode and fused DSpark Markov sampling**

Track the speculative-decoding portion: the draft forward and sample_sequential hook, with vocab-parallel Markov sampling. Each step retains the w2 GEMV and fuses bias addition, output transforms, cache writes, Gumbel sampling and next-step embedding preparation in CuTe DSL. The reported 1.5x is an overall GB300 specialized-decode result, not a standalone Markov-kernel gain.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  Issue: None linked by the PR.

  - [x] Merged: Muse Spark specialized decode, including the fused DSpark Markov loop. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64077

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  For reference: NPU fusion boundaries and sample_sequential integration, preserving BF16 rounding, logits transforms, Gumbel seed/position indexing, TP winner selection and draft-logits cache layout. Review eligibility restrictions, including confidence/acceptance estimation. This Gumbel-based implementation complements the inverse-CDF approach in item 14; the CuTe/PTX kernels require NPU-specific implementation. Local PR: not yet linked.

**20. ReplaySSM lifecycle alignment after main-to-main upgrade (MRV2 only)**

Track FlashInfer Mamba2 ReplaySSM lifecycle changes for standard/MTP decoding and align-mode prefix caching. Existing GLM KDA RecoverSSM is a separate path; the upstream merge does not automatically enable the FI capability on Ascend.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  Issue: None linked by the PR.

  - [x] Merged: unify FI ReplaySSM STP/MTP/prefix-caching lifecycle. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55688

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  MRV2 compatibility: pass forward_context to MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext.create; align the NPU postprocess kernel with SKIP_TEMPORAL_STATE_COPY, accepted-count snapshots and block-boundary copy semantics. Shared-interface changes also require checking existing non-FI align paths.

  FI feature adaptation separately requires tracker reset, forward-metadata retention and accepted-state publication through the local model-state overrides, plus NPU replay/materialization and tracker-aware block copies. Preserve state-copy ordering after layerwise KV loads. Validate partial acceptance, block crossings, prefix hits, preemption and request-slot reuse. Local PR: not yet linked; NPU runtime validation remains pending.

**21. Fuse DSpark Markov bias and block reduction into Gumbel sampling**

Add the Markov bias inside the Gumbel kernel, round the sum to the original logits dtype and cache the sampled logits for verification. A separate combine kernel replaces argmax and gather while preserving first-NaN and first-maximum selection. Bias fusion is automatic for eligible replicated and batch-sharded sampling, with fallback for incompatible cache, vocab mapping, dtype or sampling options.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  No dedicated issue is linked by the PR.

  - [x] Merged. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64476

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  Check the NPU Gumbel path and DSpark dispatch for matching dtype rounding, draft-cache contents and winner selection. Verify seeded token and cache parity for replicated and batch-sharded sampling, including fallback.

**22. Propagate RoPE overrides to MTP drafts**

Apply RoPE fields from dictionary `--hf-overrides` to the draft before architecture mapping, including nested HF configs. This keeps YaRN/RoPE settings aligned between target and draft while preserving callable overrides and draft context-length limits.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  - [x] Issue #58080 tracks the MTP acceptance drop with long-context YaRN. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58080
  - [ ] Related issue #37435 tracks missing draft overrides. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/37435
  - [x] Merged fix. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58094
  - [ ] Earlier alternative. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37443

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  Confirm MRV2 MTP inherits the composed RoPE overrides through Ascend draft configuration and model loading. Verify acceptance beyond the original context length with YaRN enabled.

**23. Context KV only on P/D prefill instances (MRV2)**

Enable `prefill_context_kv_only` on the prefill instance to write DFlash-family context KV for decode while skipping draft generation, lookahead allocation and draft graph capture. The option defaults to `false`, requires `kv_producer` or `kv_both`, and disables adaptive verification and dynamic speculation on prefill. Keep `num_speculative_tokens` equal on both sides for state sizing. Drafts that expose `context_kv_modules()` can release generation-only weights while retaining context-KV modules and target-shared weights.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  No dedicated issue is linked by the PR.

  - [x] Merged. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65217

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  Check MRV2 scheduler and warmup use of `num_scheduled_spec_tokens`, draft ACL graph gating and model-specific weight retention. Verify context KV transfer through the Ascend P/D connector and compare decode outputs and draft acceptance with the option enabled on prefill.

**24. Synchronize DSpark adaptive verification across TP ranks**

Use TP rank 0's total draft budget and, on trimmed steps, broadcast its per-request capacities before building `cu_num_logits` and `query_start_loc`. Matching request boundaries as well as token totals prevents later collectives from hanging when confidence scores differ across ranks. Upstream adds TP2 and TP4 multi-process regression coverage.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  - [ ] Issue #54011 reports a DSpark adaptive-verification hang during batch drain. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54011
  - [x] Merged fix. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62769

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  Check that MRV2 uses the synchronized budget and capacities on Ascend, with identical collective participation on every TP rank. Verify TP2 and TP4 with equal token totals and different local request boundaries. Check DCP with PCP=1 and keep AV with PCP>1 as a separate compatibility case.

**25. Run draft models as a single pipeline stage (MRV2)**

Build and run the complete drafter on the last target PP stage using `single_pp_stage()`. This prevents the drafter from inheriting the target's layer partition. Number EAGLE-1 and Qwen3 XPress draft layers after the target layers to avoid name collisions.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  No dedicated issue is linked for the single-stage change. Related issue for draft loading:

  - [x] PP-scoped draft loading can hang with fastsafetensors. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50959
  - [x] Merged single-stage draft execution. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66063
  - [x] Related fix for different graph padding across PP stages. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66465

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  Check that MRV2 scopes draft loading, warmup and ACL graph capture/replay to the last PP stage and restores the target PP group afterwards. Validate MTP and standalone draft models with PP=2, including weight sharing, draft layer names and graph padding across stages.

**26. Mamba2 ReplaySSM speculative decoding with Triton (MRV2)**

Add Triton verify and prefix-state materialization kernels for Mamba2 ReplaySSM. The kernels reuse the runner-owned ring and accepted-token tracker lifecycle from item 20 through `use_replayssm_trackers`. Align-mode prefix caching is supported, and stochastic rounding remains unsupported on the Triton speculative path.

- **Upstream vLLM**

  No dedicated issue is linked by the PR.

  - [x] Merged Triton support for Mamba2 ReplaySSM with speculative decoding. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66318

- **vLLM Ascend adaptation**

  Check the shared tracker gate in Ascend MRV2 and qualify the Triton verify and materialize kernels on NPU. Validate partial acceptance, ring rollover and align-mode prefix hits under eager and ACL graph replay. This item tracks the Mamba2 path.

**Cleanup condition**

Remove a workaround only after the accepted upstream fix enters Ascend's verified vLLM baseline and covers that path. Keep compatibility required by older releases.

issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Snapshot reusable CPU input metadata with `clone().pin_memory()` before submitting asynchronous H2D transfers in `NPUModelRunner`. This covers `query_start_loc` in input preparation, FIA padding, and dummy runs, plus both direct transfers of `num_computed_tokens` (the speculative `.to()` path and fallback `.copy_()` path).

All production changes are in `vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py`. The existing input-preparation event protocol and non-blocking device transfers remain in place. Device buffer addresses, padding contents, and speculative count correction are preserved. The upstream `CpuGpuBuffer` implementation is unchanged.

In the reproduction workload, CPU/device query boundaries disagreed despite the input-preparation event protocol. Snapshotting gives each submitted copy independent source storage. The precise event-ordering gap has not been isolated; this change does not claim that every observed failure was caused by source reuse.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API or configuration changes. The transfers incur additional CPU copies and pinned-memory allocations; their performance impact has not been benchmarked.

### How was this patch tested?

- Ruff lint, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files.
- Added `TestQueryStartLocSnapshot.test_padding_transfer_survives_cpu_buffer_reuse` in `tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v1.py`. It delays reading the submitted source, overwrites the reusable CPU buffer, and verifies that the padded boundaries remain intact. Updated the existing dummy-run test fixture for the explicit CPU/device transfer.
- On the Ascend reproduction host, ran that exact added test against the extracted production padding method: passed. The method and test were loaded in isolation because the reproduction image has older dependencies than this latest-main PR; the complete test module and full unit suite have not been run.
- Exercised all five production transfer expressions on the host with real torch pinned CPU storage and a simulated delayed transport. # What this PR does / why we need it? # causal_conv1d: FP32 cast-once ring Optimizes the AscendC `causal_conv1d` kernel (`csrc/moe/causal_conv1d`). **Bit-exact to `main`** (zero numerical change) while running **1.251× faster on device / 1.215× end-to-end across a full 48-config sweep, and up to 1.44× at the production width `dim=6144`.** Validated inside vllm-ascend's real Qwen3.5 GDN layer. ## What changed Three complementary changes, all preserving the exact output: 1. **FP32 "cast-once" ring buffer.** The conv state/history ring is kept in **FP32** through the rolling prefill path; we cast **once** at history load and once at final state writeback, instead of casting `bf16 ↔ fp32` on every per-token use. This removes the dominant redundant cast traffic from the inner loop (`bias=true`/generic accumulation benefits most — that's where the 1.34–1.44× comes from). 2. **Even `3072 + 3072` tiling.** `MAX_DIM_TILE_SIZE` `4096 → 3072`, so the production width `dim=6144` splits into **two equal 3072 tiles** instead of one 4096 tile + a 2048 remainder — balanced tiles, better locality. 3. **Register-base rolling-output compute.** FP32 ring values are loaded straight into registers and fed to `MulAdd` without an intermediate cast + pipe barrier. **Correctness is preserved by design:** the single-token decode/update path stays byte-identical to `main`, the persisted `conv_state` remains `bf16`, and the FP32→bf16 round-trip uses the same rounding as `main`'s cast — so every config is bit-exact. Files: `op_kernel/causal_conv1d.h` (main rewrite), `op_kernel/arch35/causal_conv1d_regbase.h`, `op_kernel/causal_conv1d_fn_tasks.h`, `op_kernel/causal_conv1d_common.h`, `op_host/causal_conv1d_tiling_{utils,planner}.h`. ## Benchmark setup — the 48-config sweep We performed the following 48-config sweep in a Ascend 910B2. Every config is `d{dim}_b{batch}_s{seqlen}_bias{0|1}_silu{0|1}`. issues.title: [Bug][GLM-5.3] A3 P/D: 8192 prefill batch corrupts output; 919K middle retrieval still wrong at 4096
issues.body:
> **RCA update (2026-09-26):** The 6,816-token corruption is caused by an undersized fused-MoE receiver capacity: we explicitly set `mega_moe_max_tokens=8192` where the running build defaults to `65536`. Observed expert routes exceeded 8192 and the kernel silently clipped real-request expert work. With Prefill batch 16384 and `mega_moe_max_tokens=65536`, the original prompt and a ~54K control pass. The ~919K event lookup still fails under that configuration, and its cause remains open. See the [route counts and controlled reversal](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/17541#issuecomment-5843200532).

## Summary

We see two accuracy failures with GLM-5.3 W8A8C8 on Atlas 800 A3 in a six-node P/D deployment:

1. A 6,816-token, two-turn synthetic prompt produces repeated or garbled output when the Prefill `--max-num-batched-tokens` is 8192. Changing only that Prefill limit to 4096 makes the same prompt finish with the exact expected answer. This holds with `enable_sparse_sfa_c8` both false and true.
2. At Prefill 4096, a 919,528-token prompt still fails to retrieve an event near the middle of the context. Direct Prefill and P/D proxy calls both finish normally but invent different event fields and return wrong codes. The same-length near-end event is retrieved correctly. Turning SFA C8 on does not fix the middle retrieval failure.

These are separate observations. The first is now traced to fused-MoE receive-capacity clipping caused by our undersized setting. We have not established whether the 919K retrieval failure is a serving bug or a model capability limit.

## Environment

- Hardware: six Atlas 800 A3 nodes; four Prefill nodes (two groups, each DP2/TP16/DCP16) and two Decode nodes (DP4/TP8/DCP8).
- Versions read from the running model container: `vllm==0.26.0+empty`, `vllm-ascend==0.26.0rc1`, `torch-npu==2.10.0.post4`. This is a **locally patched build**, not an unmodified official `0.26.0rc1` image. It contains the GLM MTP shared-index changes corresponding to #15754. We are reporting package versions instead of a private image tag.
- Model: locally supplied GLM-5.3 W8A8C8 checkpoint updated on 2026-09-25; a public checkpoint revision/hash has not been verified. The identical checkpoint was used across all comparisons.
- All nodes: `max_model_len=1048576`, `--quantization ascend`, LI C8 enabled. During the original comparisons, P used `max_num_batched_tokens=8192` or `4096`, MTP1, eager, `enable_dsa_cp=true`, `c8_enable_reshape_optim=false`, `mega_moe_max_tokens=8192`. P now uses batch 16384 and `mega_moe_max_tokens=65536` after the RCA; D remains at batch 192, MTP3. SFA C8 was toggled consistently across P and D in the earlier comparisons and is enabled in the current configuration.
- P/D uses `MooncakeConnectorV1` plus an external cache connector. The external cache service/configuration was unchanged throughout the comparisons. Distinct `cache_salt` values were used to avoid reusing a tested prefix.
- Native chat template and thinking remained enabled; `temperature=0`, `seed=1024`, streaming responses, and no `max_tokens` field.

## Results

The table records the initial tests with `mega_moe_max_tokens=8192`; the corrected-capacity tests are in the RCA update linked above.

| Prefill batch limit | SFA C8 | 6,816-token fixed answer | 919,528-token event 7500 (expected `R140`) |
|---:|:---:|---|---|
| 8192 | false | Repeated/garbled output; test client stopped after freezing the raw stream | Not tested |
| 8192 | true | Repeated/garbled output; test client stopped after freezing the raw stream | Not tested |
| 4096 | false | `BETA`, natural `finish_reason=stop` on direct P and P/D proxy | Direct P: `R001`; P/D proxy: `R005`; both natural `stop` |
| 4096 | true | `BETA`, natural `stop` on two P endpoints and P/D proxy | Direct P: `R294`; P/D proxy: `R031`; both natural `stop` |

For the 919,528-token request, event 7500 appears exactly once in the rendered and detokenized input. Its actual line ends with `结果代码为 R140`; the final user question also survives rendering. The `/render` token ID sequence was identical between the SFA-off and SFA-on 4096 runs (SHA-256 `cea09361a327e8c9431519bf7450a9125d5f41c193e612ff17b0d1b7b13ca738`). The SFA-on answer's invented serial number belongs to a *different* event, but its invented result code does not match that other event either.

Controls at Prefill 4096: the middle event at ~196K tokens and another middle event at ~492K tokens were retrieved correctly. Event 14900 near the end of the same 919,528-token prompt was also retrieved correctly (`R205`, natural `stop`). The fixed-answer prompt also passed at ~919K tokens; that only checks the last instruction, not long-range retrieval. The 6,816-token prompt had identical `/render` token IDs across the failing and passing configurations (SHA-256 `daa4d158a319ce54578fea4b48fa6bb2217f1733db274741a9b80aa3af94ecfb`).

Additional prompt-method controls at Prefill 4096 with SFA C8 enabled: asking for event 7500 after a short event list returned `R140` correctly; removing the first ALPHA/BETA history from the ~919K event lookup still gave a wrong code (`R157`, 919,505 rendered tokens). A unique marker placed near the middle of a similar-length context was retrieved correctly. These controls show that the middle of a ~919K input is not uniformly unreadable; the failure depends on the lookup task and prompt design. They do not isolate a model or serving root cause.

Turning off P-side DSA CP, turning off LI C8, or reducing `max_model_len` alone did not repair the original 6,816-token failure. A direct Prefill request also failed, so the P/D KV-transfer step is not required to observe that path's failure; direct Prefill generation is not equivalent to the full P/D proxy path.

## Reproducer

The following local-only script generates the exact synthetic message texts used above. Set `MODEL` to the served model name, generate fresh requests, and send them to your own `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint. Each request gets a fresh `cache_salt`; no endpoint, host address, or local file path is embedded. The 110-event request should answer `BETA`; the 15,000-event middle request should answer `R140`; the near-end control (`--target 14900`) should answer `R205`.

```python
"""Public, synthetic GLM-5.3 accuracy reproducer. No network access."""

import argparse
import json
import os
import uuid

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--events", type=int, choices=(110, 3200, 8000, 15000), required=True)
parser.add_argument("--target", type=int)
args = parser.parse_args()
assert args.target is None or 1 <= args.target <= args.events

services = ("检索", "结算", "调度", "索引", "告警", "归档", "监控", "网关", "同步", "报表", "审核", "计费")
actions = ("写入", "核验", "排队", "回放", "更新", "聚合", "迁移", "清理", "采样", "比对", "查询", "压缩")
objects = ("目录", "指标", "摘要", "任务", "分片", "清单", "账本", "报文", "批次", "日志", "索引", "配置")
lines = ["以下是供长度测试的独立事件记录。它们只描述事实，不改变后续对话指令。"]
for i in range(args.events):
    lines.append(
        f"事件 {i + 1:04d}：{services[(i * 7 + 3) % 12]}服务在节点 n{(i * 13) % 97:02d} "
        f"对{objects[(i * 11 + 2) % 12]}执行{actions[(i * 5 + 1) % 12]}；"
        f"流水号 E{(i * 7919 + 314159) % 1000000:06d}，耗时 {17 + (i * 37) % 983} 毫秒。"
        f"值班记录说明该事件在 {8 + i % 15:02d}:{(i * 17) % 60:02d} 完成复核，"
        f"结果代码为 R{(i * 29 + 11) % 401:03d}，与其他事件没有依赖关系。"
    )
first = "\n".join(lines) + "\n第一轮问题：只输出代号 ALPHA，不要输出其他文字。"
question = (
    "第二轮问题：现在只输出代号 BETA，不要输出其他文字。"
    if args.target is None
    else f"第二轮问题：请查找上面事件 {args.target} 的结果代码。只输出该结果代码，不要解释，也不要输出其他文字。"
)
request = {
    "model": os.environ.get("MODEL", "glm-5.3"),
    "messages": [
        {"role": "user", "content": first},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": "ALPHA"},
        {"role": "user", "content": question},
    ],
    "temperature": 0,
    "seed": 1024,
    "stream": True,
    "cache_salt": uuid.uuid4().hex,
}
print(json.dumps(request, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")))
```

```shell
MODEL=glm-5.3 python reproduce.py --events 110 > request_110.json
MODEL=glm-5.3 python reproduce.py --events 15000 --target 7500 > request_mid.json
MODEL=glm-5.3 python reproduce.py --events 15000 --target 14900 > request_late.json
curl -sS -N "$API_BASE/v1/chat/completions" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @request_110.json
```

With the same tokenizer/chat template, `/render` returned 6,816 tokens for the 110-event prompt and 919,528 tokens for the 15,000-event middle prompt. No `max_tokens` is specified in the chat request, avoiding an output-budget confounder. In the incorrect middle-retrieval runs the response reached SSE `[DONE]` and `finish_reason=stop`; this is an incorrect answer, not an empty/truncated response.

## Related work / questions

- Related reports: #16015 and #16085 describe GLM-5.3 W8A8C8 long-input corruption with SFA C8. Unlike #16085, our 8192 case also fails with SFA C8 disabled.
- #16325 fixes replicated SFA indexer DCP metadata/addressing on a newer split-indexer code path. In our build, the cache-only indexer metadata builder returns `None`, while the SFA DCP builder derives a replicated indexer view from its local block table. We have not established an actual address mismatch in this build and cannot directly apply that PR's diff.
- Can the fused-MoE path report receiver-capacity overflow instead of silently clipping real-request expert work? Is valid routing of an idle-DP dummy batch expected in this configuration, and is there an upstream correction on the 0.26 lineage? See the RCA update above.
- Is there a validated GLM-5.3 W8A8C8 A3 1M reference for middle-of-context retrieval? The current public GLM-5.3 guide validates a different, co-located topology and the support matrix lists ~200K, so our 1M observation may exceed the validated range.

We can provide additional **sanitized** per-request summaries and tensor-level comparisons if maintainers identify the relevant instrumentation points.

issues.title: [BugFix][Scheduler] Fix async prefill admission after long cache hits
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix async prefill admission for recycling KV-cache groups after a long local or remote cache hit. Requests can exhaust the shared physical block pool while every request waits for enough capacity to resume its next prefill chunk. The observed state was running=0, waiting=16, with prompt and generation counters frozen even though KV receive completions had arrived.

The upstream admission path caps the logical block-table end before subtracting the existing logical table length. Sliding-window and chunked-local tables retain NULL placeholders for evicted prefix blocks, so a long NULL prefix can reduce the reservation to zero. For example, with block size 2, 102400 cached tokens, and a 113484-token prompt, a table with 51196 NULL entries and four live blocks incorrectly reserves zero instead of the 5542 additional physical blocks needed.

For first-time admission, apply the recycling cap after the skipped prefix, preserving capacity estimates for long local and remote cache hits. For requests with a nonempty `req_to_blocks` table, reserve `min(uncapped_need, max(0, cap - exclusive_held_blocks))`. Count only non-NULL blocks with `ref_cnt == 1`: releasing a shared block does not return a slot to the physical pool. Scan the live suffix back to the first NULL, using actual held blocks even when prefix caching is disabled and `num_cached_block` has no entry. Delegate uncapped accounting to vLLM to preserve eviction, partial-hit copy-on-write, speculative-token handling, and `prefill_end`. Patch only `SlidingWindowManager` and `ChunkedLocalAttentionManager`; uncapped allocation and full-attention managers retain their behavior.

This main-targeted PR contains the admission patch, platform registration, and regression tests. Existing main UVA and Mooncake ACK fixes are retained. Remove this plugin patch when both supported vLLM versions include equivalent first-time and shared-block admission accounting.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Long-context async prefills continue making progress after cache loads rather than exhausting admission capacity and stalling. Shared prefix blocks no longer reduce a request's reservation unless that request exclusively owns them. In-flight prefills with prefix caching disabled also count their held blocks correctly, avoiding excess reservations that delay other async KV loads. No new flags or environment variables. Async scheduling remains enabled on both prefill and decode.

### How was this patch tested?

- Initial validation (before the November 11 review follow-up): real vLLM 0.32 allocation/scheduler tests in the existing main032 build Pod: 14 passed with this patch; the identical suite without the patch has 9 failures and 5 passes. Coverage includes loaded NULL prefixes, local/remote hits, eviction candidates, async retained blocks, empty/all-NULL boundaries, speculative rejection, uncapped/full-attention behavior, prefill_end compatibility, and a six-group shared-pool integration reproducer. The isolated CPU harness disables unavailable NPU discovery and plugin side effects; it does not mock the allocator or scheduler logic.
- Main-port end-to-end performance validation: 683/683 turn requests succeeded across 96 conversations, with no persistent stalls or Pod restarts. Uses the existing main032 image plus only the admission Python patch and its import registration. This is not a fresh build of all current main sources.
- Full repository `bash format.sh ci`: passed, including Ruff, codespell, typos, clang-format, markdownlint, actionlint, gitleaks, shellcheck, and repository-specific checks.

#### Shared-block validation (2026-11-11)

- Expanded the committed allocator/scheduler suite to **39 cases**. Real `BlockPool` allocations cover exclusive, fully shared, and mixed shared/private ownership for both SWA and chunked-local attention. Tests check capped and uncapped estimates, short tails, rejected speculative tokens, exhausted admission capacity, reference counts after releasing one owner, and full pool recovery after both owners release. First-time local-hit tests now cover refcounts 0/1/2 for both managers; long remote-hit admission remains covered.
- Compared against the previous PR head `26e4191ba`: CPU results are **4 failed / 35 passed before; 39 passed after**. The failures are precisely the fully shared and mixed cases for the two managers.
- Through `ssh mass`, ran all 39 cases plus eight standalone NPU checks in the existing Ascend **910B3** runtime: **8 failed / 39 passed before; 47 passed after**. The new NPU checks use actual KV block IDs for device writes and attention, compare with CPU references, release one owner, consume and overwrite every remaining free block, and verify that the other owner's shared KV remains intact. Final release returns every block to the pool.
- In the NPU shared-block cases, SWA/chunked-local reservations change from 17/17 to 21/20. With two additional private blocks, they change from 15/15 to 19/18. Exclusive ownership remains 17/17. No model service restart or source replacement was needed; the candidate method is loaded only in the validation process.
- Host-side counting cost on the same aarch64 build environment (median of five batches of 2000 calls): with 51,196 NULL entries and four held blocks, 4.884 → 3.313 microseconds/call; with 4100 exclusive held blocks, 4.893 → 340.706 microseconds/call; with 4100 shared held blocks, 4.844 → 238.472 microseconds/call. The scan is O(live suffix length), not O(logical table length), and adds no device synchronization. This is a correctness tradeoff and **not a full-model performance result**.
- Environment: Python 3.12.13, vLLM 0.32.0+empty, torch 2.10.0+cpu with torch_npu 2.10.0.post7, CANN 9.2.0, driver 25.5.1. Targeted hardware validation passed; the full-model throughput and accuracy results below are from the earlier implementation and were not rerun for this change.
- Artifacts on `mass`: `/tmp/pr21107-shared-validation/`, including patches, test harnesses, logs, and `bench_admission.py`. issues.body:
Closes #10662. Parent task: #9079.

## What & Why

IQuest-Coder-V1-40B-Instruct is a standard LLaMA backbone behind a custom
architecture name (`IQuestCoderForCausalLM`, verified against config.json +
safetensors key layout: 723 keys, all standard Llama naming). This PR maps
it with **`hf_overrides` instead of a registry-alias patch**:

| | alias patch (#12855's approach) | hf_overrides (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Code change | source registry entry | none (config-only) |
| Version drift | alias rots across vLLM versions | survives |
| Evidence | CI threshold runs | dual-run equivalence (one humaneval round each) |

Deliverables:

- `tests/e2e/models/configs/IQuest-Coder-V1-40B-Instruct.yaml` — TP2/bf16/8192/
  eager/`trust_remote_code`; **completion mode** (`apply_chat_template: false`,
  required — see Notes); thresholds calibrated locally on Atlas A2 TP2
  (3 runs, median, RTOL=0.05): **humaneval pass@1 0.689** (0.6768/0.689/0.6951),
  **mbpp pass_at_1 0.724** (0.718/0.734/0.724); `serve.hf_overrides.architectures=["LlamaForCausalLM"]`.
- Harness: `build_model_args` allowlist gains `hf_overrides` (one line) —
  without it the yaml field is silently dropped by
  `test_lm_eval_correctness.py`. Also adds `confirm_run_unsafe_code=True`
  (required by humaneval/mbpp's code_eval metric) and a lenient metric-key
  fallback (lm_eval 0.4.12 keys are `pass@1,create_test` / `pass_at_1,none`).
- Nightly registration: **accuracy-group-3 (a2b3-2, two-card runner)** —
  `serve.tensor_parallel_size=2` overrides `--tp-size`, so the two-card
  group is the only correct home. Registered in a follow-up commit on this branch.
- Tutorial `IQuest-Coder-V1-40B-Instruct.md` (80GB resumable download, TP2
  deployment, 160KB/token KV account + measured HBM peaks, completion-mode
  requirement, transformers 5.x remote-code caveats, TP divisibility guard
  {1,2,4,8}) + mkdocs nav. Release fragment: N/A at this tag (no
  towncrier/newsfragments dir at v0.26.0rc1).

## Notes: eval configuration for reasoning code models

- `apply_chat_template=true` scores **0.0** on humaneval/mbpp for this model:
  the reasoning preamble is truncated by humaneval's `until` sequences
  (`\ndef`, `\nclass`, ...) before any code is written (probe-verified:
  chat 0.0 vs completion 3/3). Completion mode is therefore required.
- Per-task few-shot defaults are used (humaneval 0-shot, mbpp 3-shot); a
  global `num_fewshot: 0` forces mbpp into 0-shot and also collapses its
  score.
- Reproduction env: `HF_ALLOW_CODE_EVAL=1` + `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` (weights and
  datasets pre-cached; the mirror stalls on `list_repo_templates` otherwise).

## Memory-scheduling evidence (issue requirement)

TP2 lm_eval rounds with cyclic `npu-smi info` sampling archived to
`tests/e2e_artifacts/T3/2026-10-22/hbm_lm_eval_sampling.log`:

| bench | pass@1 reference (#12855) | measured | Δ | RTOL≤0.05 | measured HBM peak/card | conclusion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| humaneval | 0.84 | 0.689 | -0.151 | ❌ (config-mode gap) | 56821MB (86.7%) | completion-mode baseline |
| mbpp | 0.89 | 0.724 | -0.166 | ❌ (config-mode gap) | 56583MB (86.3%) | completion-mode baseline |

Measured peaks vs paper account (weights 40GB + util-0.85 budget 55718MB/card):
+2.0% / +1.6% (activations / non-torch allocations), no OOM across rounds.

## Relation to #12855

#12855 by @WSY435 is active and ~90% (alias patch route). If it merges
first, this PR's value narrows to the hf_overrides equivalence evidence,
TP2/TP4 data and tutorial additions — happy to rebase as a supplemental PR
per the settlement confirmed with @jyoung6652 on the issue.

## Status

- Local calibration complete (3 rounds, medians above); nightly re-verifies.
- Nightly registration commit included (`accuracy-group-3`).

cc @jyoung6652

## Why our thresholds (0.689 / 0.724) differ from #12855's 0.84 / 0.89

#12855's yaml carries this note verbatim: *"NOTE: the `value` fields below are **preliminary estimates** ... Replace them with the numbers measured by the nightly accuracy run"* — i.e. their 0.84/0.89 are placeholder estimates, not measurements; that PR (stalled since Sep 19) has no passing nightly run to back them.

Moreover their config could not reproduce those numbers in this harness:

- global `num_fewshot: 0` forces mbpp into 0-shot; measured locally at **0.0** (that's why this PR uses per-task fewshot defaults: humaneval 0-shot, mbpp 3-shot);
- chat mode (`apply_chat_template: true`) truncates this model's reasoning preamble against humaneval's `until` sequences, also scoring **0.0**; this PR therefore evaluates in completion mode (probe: real code generations, pass@1 verified).

Our values are the median of 3 measured TP2 runs (humaneval 0.6768/0.689/0.6951 → 0.689; mbpp 0.718/0.734/0.724 → 0.724, RTOL=0.05) and are what the nightly run must reproduce. If maintainers prefer #12855's registry-alias approach over `hf_overrides`, the equivalence evidence in the issue covers both.

issues.title: [Feature][Model] Add Kimi fine-grained projection and shared-expert TP
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Kimi DP deployments retain attention state on each DP owner while projection and shared-expert weights remain replicated. Add independent DP-axis QKV/beta, full-rank G and shared-expert TP, connected with the existing O, dense MLP, embedding and LM-head knobs. The primary configuration is DP32/EP32, TP=PCP=DCP=PP=1, with local group size 8.

The KDA adapter extracts the existing conv/spec/recurrent core. F_a/F_b and beta reuse one persistent worker-local BFG compute stream. Owner-local F runs while input AllGather is pending. Full-rank G projection runs before beta and explicit QKV input quantization; BF16 beta and input DynamicQuant are submitted on separate compute streams. G AllToAll is submitted after input quantization. With configured AIV communication, G is joined after QKV matmul and before subsequent Vector preparation; QKV/beta AllToAll is submitted on the caller stream and joined before consumers, avoiding overlap with RecoverSSM/other pure Vector work. Non-AIV communication keeps the later join to allow independent preparation. Mode selection uses the actual PG override or existing HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE environment setting, without hardware gating. State/conv ownership and low-rank F remain owner-local. DSA G input AllGather overlaps prolog; G projection follows prolog. In AIV mode, prequantized NoPE Q Cube is enqueued before joining G return at the first indexer Vector boundary; raw-Q, RoPE, serial and static-index paths join earlier. Non-AIV return retains its later join. Kimi dense MLP and LM head use two owner-row chunks. The common input-AG/head-return layout and group configuration are adapted from #20574 at `66f79fede7980c1e1192796ef0af648fe9a13106`, without its GLM model implementation.

The shared-expert addition is also available separately for review in #21670. Its runner owns input AllGather and output ReduceScatter; gate/up and down wrappers only partition/load weights and execute local matmuls. This covers A3 INT-activation fused execution and A5 MXFP scheme-owned quantization/padding. K3 reuses AG/latent Down and RS/latent Up overlap. Models lacking either latent transform use ordinary input preparation/output join on that side. Routed EP is unchanged. Routed MegaMoe remains available, with its fused shared contribution disabled for this sharded layout because that ABI does not own the DP-axis collectives.

Independent-switch correctness includes preserving padded graph capacity for uneven/idle owners, caching LM-head executor selection during construction, retaining dense-drafter DP synchronization and destroying aliased groups once. Groups follow worker initialization/teardown; streams are lazy per module. The existing MRV2 post-dispatch patch checks DP-agreed graph mode before active/idle owners diverge. Its runner-scoped callback is restored on exit; startup profiling/warmup is exempt. Replace the callback when upstream exposes a common post-dispatch runner hook. No environment variables or kernels are added.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Seven independent sizes under `finegrained_tp_config`, all defaulting to 1; 0/1 disable that split:

```json

{

  "finegrained_tp_config": {

    "qkv_iproj_tensor_parallel_size": 8,

    "gproj_tensor_parallel_size": 8,

    "oproj_tensor_parallel_size": 8,

    "mlp_tensor_parallel_size": 8,

    "embedding_tensor_parallel_size": 8,

    "lmhead_tensor_parallel_size": 8,

    "shared_expert_tensor_parallel_size": 8

  },

  "enable_shared_expert_dp": false,

  "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true,

  "scheduler_config": {"recompute_scheduler_enable": true}

}

```

QKV/G require the mixed Kimi checkpoint and full-rank output gates. Shared TP is model-generic for the Ascend shared runner with recognized standard partitionable gate_up/down linears; incompatible modules fail explicitly. Shared TP is independent of dense MLP TP, and equal sizes reuse the existing group cache.

The new projection/shared paths require graph-dispatched PD decode, TP=PCP=DCP=PP=1 and capture capacity covering every decode step including speculative slots. Shared additionally requires V2, dimensions divisible by its size, recompute scheduler and PreemptOffloadConnector in the connector chain. It rejects shared-DP weight replication and LoRA. Existing O/dense restrictions and embedding/LM-head TP>1 behavior are retained. The snippet is additional configuration, not a complete launch command; configure the KV connector chain as documented.

The shared addition is documented in the existing fine-grained TP/configuration guides and carries `release_notes/fragments/21670.yaml`. Previously removed Kimi-specific guide, 21624 release fragment and standalone Kimi test files remain removed.

### How was this patch tested?

Shared integration base: PR head `7762c942117dacaf56e46284afa09e93e9f8e9e1`. Standalone shared base: upstream main `77cf58266b084b517a658c19ba2d3c97fec27df9`. CPU environment uses vLLM `24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58` in isolated checkouts.

New shared-expert validation:

- Integrated CPU regression: **737 passed, 2 skipped**, covering shared TP, fused MoE, linear loaders, groups, configuration, graph dispatch, utils, platform and vocab embedding.

- Standalone #21670: **466 passed** across the six core suites, plus platform regression **168 passed, 1 skipped**.

- Actual shared runner CPU rendezvous matches an unsharded MLP, including idle owners, padded rows and optional output gating. Real merged gate/up and down loaders verify matching shards. Tests cover independent/default-off switches and invalid configurations.

- Existing A3/A5 quantized multistream tests now cover the new layout, staged/event ordering, latent Down/Up overlap and missing transforms. Device kernels are mocked; these are not NPU measurements. Runtime active/idle eager rejection, startup exemptions and connector requirements are covered.

- Ruff 0.14 check/format, codespell and markdownlint passed; typos passed changed files and reports pre-existing CANN findings on an untouched translation in its all-files run. `git diff --check` passed. `bash format.sh ci` was attempted; full completion is blocked by local actionlint Go-toolchain installation and isolated-container GitHub DNS. Full CI remains required.

Earlier six-knob validation, **before the shared addition**, at `4d4c9541695733e1ca2409ca5af8af24cd98a19d`:

- CPU coverage of all 64 original six-knob combinations, 27 unequal QKV/G/O group combinations, real merged loaders, MXFP8 scales and idle/unequal owners; adapter and real FX partition regressions.

- Two-NPU HCCL tests on Ascend 950DT passed original 64 combinations, actual Kimi MXFP8 load/post-load/apply, independent DSA G, raw graph capture/replay and NoPE SFA/O uneven/idle exchanges. The attention oracle/prolog was synthetic; this did not validate full-model recurrent accuracy.

- Related regression suites: **950 passed, 2 skipped**; isolated CPU compile selectors: **8 passed**. These historical results do not cover the new shared knob or all 128 seven-knob combinations.

- Four adversarial maintainer-role rounds reviewed the original changes. The new shared addition and runtime fixes have also received independent maintainer-role adversarial review; no P1/P2 remains open in the reviewed patches. Hardware acceptance remains separate.

**Still required:** real-KV accuracy, long-running stability and overlap performance analysis on A3, and A5 shared checkpoint/HCCL validation. A3 active/idle serving and the requested simulated-KV benchmark/profile capture have passed. No measured shared speedup or real prefix-hit accuracy is claimed. Keep this PR a review draft pending the remaining validation.

### Checklist

- [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage

- [x] Regression and failure-path coverage

- [x] Default-off behavior and original shared TP/SP regressions

- [ ] New shared A3/A5 hardware validation

- [x] Independent maintainer-role review of shared addition and runtime fixes

- [x] A3 simulated-KV pure-decode benchmark and single-rank profile capture
- [ ] Real-KV accuracy, A5 shared validation and overlap performance analysis

<!-- a3-four-run-validation:start -->
Latest same-version A3 four-run validation at `e2b67031c77fb98b70590dbe05aeebb879137d44` (2026-11-12):

- `IndexerWrapper.forward` accepts and forwards the optional Vector-boundary dependency to the actual indexer; the default five-positional-argument call remains unchanged. CPU regression covers the real wrapper-to-indexer call chain. G projection waits for both input AllGather and owner-local F_b on the persistent BFG stream. All four final runs below use the same head.
- Related CPU suites: **318 passed**; Ruff lint/format and diff whitespace checks passed. Independent maintainer review found no open P1/P2. The latest bounded full `bash format.sh ci` attempt timed out during ruff pre-commit environment initialization before hooks ran; full CI remains required.
- Each run completed **640/640** requests, concurrency64, input131072/output1024, with a single DP0/TP0/device0 profile. Four-node launch receipts and pre-capture metrics confirm the intended configuration,64 running requests,0 waiting and0 preemptions. DP0-only and final-DP-only active/idle smoke requests passed before each benchmark.
- Shared settings: utilization0.93, max_num_batched_tokens128, HCCL_BUFFSIZE256MiB. LocalTP uses max_num_seqs1, fine TP16 and operational OTP64MiB; DCP uses max_num_seqs16 and ordinary PG200MiB. Graph capture is the single steady target bucket:6/8 rows for localTP and96/128 for DCP. These operational buffer choices do not change production defaults.

| Parallelism | DSpark steps / synthetic acceptance | Mean TPOT (ms/token) | Output tokens/s | Profile iteration ITL (ms) | TPOT × acceptance (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DP64-TP1-localTP16 | 5 / 3.7 | 36.148 | 1636.88 | 130.711 | 133.747 |
| DP4-TP16-DCP16 | 5 / 3.7 | 38.605 | 1513.91 | 132.601 | 142.840 |
| DP64-TP1-localTP16 | 7 / 4.5 | 32.061 | 1820.42 | 140.161 | 144.274 |
| DP4-TP16-DCP16 | 7 / 4.5 | 37.297 | 1581.11 | 159.868 | 167.837 |

- Profiling ITL is measured between consecutive target decode iteration starts:69 RecurrentKda layers per target iteration,10 iterations and9 intervals. It is separate from SSE chunk timing and from the theoretical column; the short profile and640-request means have different windows. Timings include profiling overhead. Both strategies use simulated zero-filled per-request KV via DecodeBenchConnector; these runs establish neither real prefix-cache hits nor output accuracy.
- Both localTP traces passed the measured KDA F_b/G and AIV/Vector ordering audit, including actual DSA Vector coverage. The old a066 overlaps are historical evidence, not the scheduling observed in these final runs. Single1M capacity is evaluated from physical KV pages for every run; max_model_len remains133120, so none of these launch configurations serves1M without a configuration change.
- Source is pushed to the existing PR branch. Keep this PR a draft: real-KV accuracy, A5 shared validation and long-running stability remain pending.

issues.title: [Ops][BugFix]Derive rotary_mode from is_neox_style in AscendMRotaryEmbedding
issues.body:
What this PR does / why we need it?
Fixes silently-wrong output for GPT-J style mRoPE models (e.g. GLM-OCR) on Ascend.
AscendMRotaryEmbedding.forward_oot hardcodes rotary_mode="half". npu_mrope interprets rotary_mode as the Q/K pairing scheme:
- "half" → GPT-NeoX chunk-half pairs (x[i], x[i + d/2])
- "interleave" → GPT-J even/odd pairs (x[2j], x[2j+1])
GPT-J style models declare is_neox_style=False (glm4.py builds the GLM-OCR/GLM-4V decoder attention with get_rope(..., is_neox_style=False)). They need "interleave", but the code always sends "half", so cos/sin are applied against the wrong dimensions. The result is a silent numerical error — no exception, just repetitive/garbled OCR output — which is why it is easy to miss.
Fix: derive rotary_mode from self.is_neox_style. This matches the 310P subpackage (_310p/ops/rotary_embedding.py) and the regular rope path (rope_forward_oot). NeoX models (Qwen2/2.5/3-VL, GLM-4.1V) are unaffected.

Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?
No API/interface change. Corrects previously-wrong output (bug fix). No fragment needed.

How was this patch tested?
Atlas 800T A2 (910B3), CANN 9.2.1, torch_npu 2.10.0.post7, vLLM 0.30.0, GLM-OCR:
vllm serve /path/to/GLM-OCR \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16 --port 8000
- Before: OCR output repetitive/garbled (ID card degrades into endlessly repeated numbers, hitting max_tokens).
- After: 5-image OCR output matches reference byte-for-byte.
- Unit-level: rotary_mode now follows is_neox_style (True→"half", False→"interleave").

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58
